To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TNF can be protective or detrimental depending upon the levels of expression.
(a) TNF can have dual actions on neurons and (b) the duality of TNFs actions is mediated by the level of activation of the TNF receptor.

chronic overexpression of moderate levels of TNF attenuates 6-OH-DA induced nigrostriatal degeneration, while chronic overexpression of high levels of TNF leads to progressive loss of nigrostriatal DA neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that underlie the dual action of TNF signaling in the CNS.
understanding the dual actions of the cytokine TNF in the brain.
the dual role of TNF signaling in the brain and the potential mechanisms that underlie these outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TNF has a dual action in the nigrostriatum and this dual action can be modulated by the level of expression of TNF and the presence of 6-OHD.
the dual actions of cytokines are a result of the interplay between multiple factors, including the type of cytokine, the level and duration of expression, and the cellular context.

TNF is not a “neurodegenerative factor” but rather a dual action factor that can have neurodegenerative and neuroprotective actions, and that these actions are dependent on the context in which it acts and the levels of TNF expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TNF signaling is a duality.

the dual effects of TNF on neuronal survival can be mediated by the same receptor and the same signaling pathway, but the balance of the two opposing effects can be tipped in favor of either one by the level of TNF and/or by the presence of a second stimulus that can either potentiate or inhibit one of the effects.
the dual actions of cytokines can be mediated by the same cytokine at the same time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to understand the mechanisms that mediate the duality of cytokine action in order to understand the role of cytokines in neurodegenerative disorders such as PD.
the duality of TNFs actions is likely a result of the complex interplay between TNF signaling and other pathways that are activated in response to injury and/or disease.
the outcome of cytokine signaling is dependent upon the cellular context in which it is activated.
